title: Lesson 8
paragraph: 問題への対応と立て直し

words.meaning: to fail to happen after being planned or agreed
words.japaneseMeaning: 計画などが実現せず流れる
words.example: The purchase may fall through if the loan is refused.

sentencePractice.prompt: The sale was almost agreed, but without the buyer’s loan it will ____ and never be completed.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Failure to complete the planned sale means it falls through. Going ahead or coming into effect indicates that it proceeds.

words.meaning: to meet an unexpected problem that slows progress
words.japaneseMeaning: 思わぬ障害にぶつかる
words.example: We hit a snag when the replacement part did not fit.

words.meaning: to return to the planned course after a delay or problem
words.japaneseMeaning: 計画どおりの状態に戻る
words.example: A revised schedule helped the project get back on track.

words.meaning: to change an unsuccessful situation into a successful one
words.japaneseMeaning: 悪い状況を好転させる
words.example: Better service helped the small shop turn things around.

words.meaning: to stop a problem at an early stage before it grows
words.japaneseMeaning: 問題の芽を早めに摘む
words.example: A quick conversation helped us nip the disagreement in the bud.
meaningDistractors: let the cat out of the bag
words.usageNote: something を the problem などに置き換えます。悪化する前に対処することが要点です。

words.meaning: to hide or ignore a problem instead of dealing with it
words.japaneseMeaning: 問題を隠して見て見ぬふりをする
words.example: The manager tried to sweep the accounting error under the carpet.
words.usageNote: 実際の掃除ではなく、問題を隠す比喩です。under the rug という形も使います。

words.meaning: an event that makes someone realize that action or change is needed
words.japaneseMeaning: 行動や変化の必要性に気付かせる出来事
words.example: The failed safety test was a wake-up call for the factory.

words.meaning: something that seems bad at first but later brings a good result
words.japaneseMeaning: 不幸に見えて後に幸いとなること
words.example: Missing that job was a blessing in disguise: I found work much closer to home.

words.meaning: having to start again because an earlier attempt failed
words.example: The design failed the test, and we were back to square one.

sentencePractice.prompt: Our only design has failed every test, so we must discard it and start the entire project again. We are ____.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Discarding the only design and restarting puts the team at the starting point, not near completion or ahead of its timetable.

words.example: The date is still up in the air because the venue has not replied.
